To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a classification-driven approach is an effective method for protein functional annotation and that data integration is essential for protein functional annotation.

a classification-driven and knowledge base system approach to protein functional prediction and analysis provides reliable and comprehensive annotation, as well as a systematic detection of annotation error, and that this approach supports biological knowledge discovery and exploration of protein functional associations.
a rule-based and knowledge-driven approach can be used to provide consistent and reliable functional annotation of proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a reliable and scalable approach for protein functional annotation and knowledge discovery, which will be of great value in the post-genomic era.
the development of computational methods and tools for large-scale and high-quality annotation of proteins and other macromolecules.
the development of a knowledge-based system for reliable protein functional annotation and the provision of a comprehensive and integrated protein resource for the research community.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PIR provides a unique integrated public resource of annotated protein sequences for functional genomics and proteomics research.

protein annotation in PIR is based on the integration of multiple sources of information and is a process that is continuously improved with the development of new methods, the accumulation of new experimental data, and the availability of new sequence data.
PIR provides an integrated resource of protein informatic tools and data for protein sequence analysis, annotation, and knowledge discovery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed an effective and efficient system for protein family classification and functional analysis, and we are building an integrated knowledge base for the analysis and discovery of protein functional associations.
PIR provides a unique resource for protein annotation and functional discovery.
we have developed an integrated resource for protein annotation and biological discovery.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the integration of protein sequence and structure information, and the integration of protein and gene information, can be used to improve the accuracy and reliability of protein function prediction and to facilitate biological knowledge discovery.
protein family classification and annotation are important for the development of a comprehensive protein knowledgebase and for the discovery of new biological functions and relationships.
the integration of sequence analysis tools, knowledge bases, and databases is critical for reliable, large-scale protein annotation.
